property_summary: For any owner a and any new owner n != a, after the current owner successfully calls transferOwnership(n), the contract's owner must be exactly n (the function body's assignment is the final effect of the guarded call); the mutant makes the guarded call leave owner at msg.sender instead, so owner != n whenever n != the caller, breaking the rule for those fuzzed inputs.

For any current owner a and any new owner n, once a successfully calls transferOwnership(n) the owner must equal exactly n and must not be altered by any guarded call's side effects; the mutant reassigns owner inside the modifier, so guarded calls can leave owner pointing at the caller rather than the last explicitly transferred value.

For any admissible owner a and target n (n != a, both nonzero), once a calls transferOwnership(n) the stored owner must be exactly n, with the guarded transfer being the sole and final writer of owner; the mutant's modifier rewrites owner to msg.sender as a side effect of every guarded call, so a guarded call can leave owner at the caller instead of the last transferred value for some fuzzed (a, n).

After the current owner transfers ownership to a new address n, a third party s with s != n must remain unauthorized: calling guarded c.owned() must revert; the mutant's modifier mutates owner as a side effect of guarded calls, so guarded calls from s succeed (stealing ownership) after any transfer.

For any two fuzzed addresses a and n, after the initial owner transfers ownership to a and a then calls transferOwnership(n), the stored owner must equal exactly n; the mutant's modifier overwrites owner to the caller inside the guarded call, so the final owner is a instead of n whenever a != n.
For any caller equal to the current owner, owned() completes successfully (does not revert); the mutant makes owned() always revert, breaking this rule.
